systems.name: Outside Substitution and Chord Transition System
systems.summary: This system governs how a single-line improviser moves between 'inside' chord-family vocabulary and 'outside' superimposed ideas over dominant chords. Its central move is borrowing arpeggios or lines from a chord a tritone, fifth, or related distance away from the target chord, then resolving back to a chord tone of the original dominant before the next harmonic change. The outside effect is time-limited — staying too long destroys it — and the resolution note is non-negotiable. Members are the melodic regions available over a dominant chord: the inside chord family, the outside superimposed chord, and the resolution landing zone. Traversal rules govern when and how to enter/exit the outside region. Modification rules govern which substitute chord is chosen and what note the line must end on.

members.name: Inside Chord Family
members.summary: Scale tones and arpeggios native to the target dominant chord and its parent harmonic field.

members.name: Outside Superimposed Chord
members.summary: A foreign chord (e.g., A7 over D7, or D7 leading to G) borrowed to create momentary harmonic tension outside the current key center.

members.name: Resolution Landing Zone
members.summary: The mandatory chord-tone endpoint of any outside line, ensuring return to the inside before the next chord change.

traversal_rules.name: Outside Entry by Chord Superimposition
traversal_rules.summary: Enter the outside region by playing small ideas from a distantly related chord (e.g., A7) over the target dominant (D7) to create an outside effect.

references.quote_excerpt: We can create a very interesting outside effect over a D7 chord by playing small A7 ideas

traversal_rules.name: Outside Duration Ceiling
traversal_rules.summary: Do not remain on the outside superimposed chord idea for too long or the outside effect collapses and becomes non-musical.

references.quote_excerpt: Do not stay on the A7 too long because you will destroy the effect

traversal_rules.name: V7-I Cadential Superimposition
traversal_rules.summary: A second outside approach constructs a mini V7-I cadence (e.g., D7 leading to G) embedded within the line over the target chord as an additional outside device.

references.quote_excerpt: second trick is also to create a cadence V7/ I just like we did before by using D7 leading to G major

traversal_rules.name: Modal Family Outside Entry
traversal_rules.summary: When a chord belongs to a modal family (e.g., D Mixolydian from Em chord family), use the related secondary dominant (B7) to create an outside line leading to the modal tonic.

references.quote_excerpt: D Mixolydian derives from Emi Chord Family, we can use also B7 ideas leading to Emi

modification_rules.name: Resolution Note Must Be Chord Tone
modification_rules.summary: Any single-line idea — inside or outside — must end on a chord tone of the target dominant chord before the harmonic change.

references.quote_excerpt: make sure that the ending note from your single line idea is a chord tone for D7

modification_rules.name: Major 7th Superimposition for Minor Resolution
modification_rules.summary: When resolving to a minor tonic (e.g., Dm7), prefer major-7th superimposed arpeggio ideas over the preceding dominant (A7) to strengthen the pull toward the minor chord.

references.quote_excerpt: major 7th superimposed ideas will work better for A7 leading to Dm7

modification_rules.name: Single-Line as Harmonic Gateway
modification_rules.summary: Chord study is not an end in itself — chords serve as the gateway to understanding harmony, which in turn enables single-line melodic fluency.

references.quote_excerpt: The chords led me to the harmony, that helped me to become a better single line player
